mechanism: A support-surface transformation is earned by first proving a repeatable contact rule several times, then breaking that exact rule with one stronger contact. The camera must cross the same physical boundary so the lower environment reads as a consequence, and the ending should hold the new medium rather than immediately resetting.

invariants.rule: Establish one subject, one travel direction and one continuous support surface.
invariants.purpose: Defines the geometry whose rule will be tested.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without a stable surface, later rupture feels arbitrary.

invariants.rule: Repeat the same localized response at multiple contact points.
invariants.purpose: Turns footfalls or touches into counted proof.
invariants.ablation_failure: One decorative reaction cannot establish a rule.

invariants.rule: Increase response density while preserving subject identity and route.
invariants.purpose: Builds pressure without changing the premise.
invariants.ablation_failure: Unrelated effects replace escalation with montage.

invariants.rule: Make one contact irreversibly breach the previously proven support rule.
invariants.ablation_failure: A random cut below has no physical handoff.

invariants.rule: Carry the camera through the same boundary and hold the new medium.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.
